Foodtech sector shines bright amid
market volatility
Foodtech stocks weathered a wild ride in Q2,
with sharp market drops in April rapidly
reversing as strong economic numbers and new
trade deals pushed indexes to record highs by
quarter’s end. While hardware-focused
segments such as kitchen tech lagged due to
lingering supply chain headaches, digital food
delivery and restaurant tech players delivered
standout performances—beating major indexes
and proving resilient against global headwinds.
DoorDash made the biggest splash, snapping up
Deliveroo in a $3.8 billion deal and expanding
further with its SevenRooms acquisition. The
move helped propel DoorDash’s share price up
35%, reflecting both investor excitement and
bullishness on the company’s global ambitions.
Across the sector, restaurant and retail tech
companies stole the show, boasting a blazing
28% median return and showing strong
momentum as consumer demand remained
robust.
Our Q2 2025 Foodtech Public Comp Sheet and
Valuation Guide tracks metrics for key publicly
traded companies that include stock
